s.t: Chuck Prophet's song opens with a cowbell, on an album where he is backed by his wife Stephanie Finch on vocals, organ and guitar.
s.q: “Jesus was a Social Drinker,” a rocking track, with a cowbell at the start; Throughout, he is backed by Stephanie Finch (Chuck's wife) -vocals, organ, guitar

s.t: PopMatters said Chuck Prophet's song mocks social prudes through a delightfully middle-brow portrayal of its subject.
s.q: "Jesus Was a Social Drinker" mocks social prudes through a delightfully middle-brow portrayal of its subject.

f.t: His band, the Mission Express, is named after a bus line that runs through his neighbourhood.
f.q: The Mission Express is Prophet's band, named after a bus line that runs through his neighborhood.

f.t: For the 2007 album Soap and Water, he gave the musicians and engineers a stake in the master recordings to motivate them.
f.q: To better motivate the various musicians and engineers who were involved in the production of this album, Prophet gave them a stake in the master recordings.

f.t: He and his co-writer Kurt Lipschutz stopped writing together between 2000 and 2010; Lipschutz joked it was a "falling out over money – there was too much of it".
f.q: Between 2000 and 2010, the duo stopped writing together due to what was jokingly described by klipschutz as “falling out over money – there was too much of it”

f.t: The title track of his 2012 album Temple Beautiful, featuring Roy Loney of the Flamin' Groovies, was proclaimed "Coolest Song in the World" on Little Steven's Underground Garage.
f.q: The title track, "Temple Beautiful" (featuring Roy Loney of the Flamin' Groovies), was proclaimed "Coolest Song in the World" on Little Steven's Underground Garage.

f.t: He re-created Waylon Jennings's 1975 album Dreaming My Dreams in full as Dreaming Waylon's Dreams, a limited edition of 1,000 printed on a circa-1930s press.
f.q: re-creates Waylon Jennings' 1975 album Dreaming My Dreams in its entirety; Dreaming Waylon's Dreams was released as a limited edition of 1000; circa 1930s printing press
